checks.name: three exact D=5 anchors, derived not recalled

detail.only_ell_1_is_rational: In x = 1/r^2 the peak solves 27/4 x^2 - 2(9/4 - L) x - L = 0. At l = 1 the discriminant is a perfect square (110.25 = 10.5^2) and x = 5/9 exactly; l = 0, 2, 3 give sqrt(13), sqrt(1621), sqrt(57). l = 1 is also the mode PR #270's two codes disagreed on.
detail.the_integral_is_elementary: dr* = dr/f cancels the f in V, leaving int_1^inf (L/r^2 + (9/4)/r^4) dr = L + 3/4 = l(l+2) + 3/2.

checks.name: only l = 1 has a rational barrier peak - proved, not checked

detail.bracketing_argument: (4m^2+3)^2 < 16m^4+28m^2+73 < (4m^2+4)^2 for m >= 4: the left is 4m^2 + 64 > 0, the right is 4m^2 > 57. Strictly between consecutive squares, hence never a square.
detail.therefore: l = 1 is the ONLY non-negative integer l with a rational barrier peak. This is a theorem, not an inference from spot checks.

checks.name: the subtracted high-frequency coefficient is the exact one

detail.why_the_exact_value_is_the_one_subtracte: If T - 1 = -i c_exact/w + O(w^-2) and a fitted c_fit != c_exact is subtracted, the remainder retains -i(c_exact - c_fit)/w and still falls only as 1/w. The subtraction exists to make the remainder O(1/w^2); using a fit would quietly defeat it.
detail.the_residual_gap_is_the_outer_boundary_c: The fitted value sits ~0.05% below the exact one, uniformly in the outer edge. That is the 1/r^4 and 1/r^6 part of V, which the centrifugal Jost condition does not capture -- a known, bounded, edge-independent shortfall rather than a truncation drift.

checks.name: the low-frequency outer matching is converged (Jost, not plane)

detail.why_this_bin_matters: It sets the DC end of the inverse transform, and therefore the numerical realisation of the int K_reg dt = -1 sum rule.
detail.what_changed: Replacing plane-wave matching with the exact centrifugal Jost solutions moved T(w -> 0) from 1.73e-06 to 4.10e-07 -- a factor of four closer to its exact value of zero -- and made the low-w spectrum independent of the outer edge instead of drifting with it.

checks.name: the real-frequency scattering is well conditioned (unitarity)

detail.why_this_is_not_the_failed_shoot: PR #270 and #274 could not converge a quasinormal frequency by shooting in real r, because for Im w < 0 the outgoing solution grows like e^{|Im w| R} and swamps the coefficient being zeroed. Here w is REAL, both e^{+-i w r*} have unit modulus, and nothing dominates anything. This is a different, well-posed problem -- not a repair of the one that failed. Unitarity to ~1e-13, imposed nowhere, is the evidence.

detail.the_exact_zero_is_a_free_error_bar: K(t) vanishes identically for t < 0, so whatever the computation returns there IS its noise floor -- no reference value needed. Any feature at t > 0 smaller than that floor is not measurable, which is how this round knows the late-time tail is out of reach.

checks.name: GATE 3 - the kernel carries the published ringdown

detail.source: Matyjasek, Phys. Rev. D 104, 084066 (2021), arXiv:2107.04815 -- continued fractions cross-checked against Hill determinants, agreeing to 11 digits
detail.scored_against_an_external_value: The comparison is with the published continued-fraction value, never with this repository's own time-domain solver. Scoring a kernel against a frequency extracted from the same machinery that produced it would not be a check.
detail.the_band_is_reported_not_the_best_row: Extraction choices move the fit, exactly as PR #274 measured for the time-domain solver. The spread is the honest statement.

checks.name: independent check - kernel convolution vs time-domain evolution

detail.what_this_exposed: The incident amplitude is only defined where the wave is free, and the residual tracks the exactly-known potential remaining beyond the launch point. PR #274 launched at r* = 6, where V ~ 0.1 -- harmless for a quasinormal frequency, since a ringdown does not care how it was excited, and fatal for a transmission ratio.
detail.an_earlier_number_was_flattered_by_cance: With plane-wave outer matching this check read 0.92% at r* = 100. That was two errors partly cancelling: the plane-wave outer condition carried its own error in the opposite direction. Under the correct Jost condition the same launch reads 2.73%, and the series converges as 1/r*_launch. The larger number is the honest one.

detail.why_the_sum_rule_is_exact: int K dt = T(w = 0), and T(0) = 0 because the centrifugal barrier reflects zero-frequency waves completely. With K = delta(t) + K_reg, that forces int K_reg dt = -1 EXACTLY. It is a constraint, not a fit, and the measured value is checked against it.
detail.what_this_says_about_rigid_exchange: A rigid exchange kernel is delta(t), possibly delayed: whatever enters leaves undistorted, and a static signal passes perfectly. The real geometry blocks a static signal COMPLETELY, and does so entirely through the memory term, which exactly cancels the instantaneous one at DC. In absolute mass the memory is about twice the delta. The memory is not a correction to rigid exchange; it is the same size as the thing it would correct.
detail.scope_of_that_claim: This is a statement about the transfer kernel of a test scalar on a fixed D = 5 Tangherlini background, per angular channel. It says what the causal geometry does. Whether any particular BAM exchange kernel is meant to approximate THIS object is a separate question this round does not settle.

missing_dc_cell.symptom: a constant -1.9e-3 under the whole kernel, at t < 0 as well as t > 0
missing_dc_cell.cause: omega sampled at right endpoints left [0, dw] uncovered; since T(0) = 0, S(0) = -1 and the omitted cell contributes about -dw/pi everywhere
missing_dc_cell.fix: midpoint sampling, which covers [0, w_max] exactly
missing_dc_cell.would_have_been_read_as: a constant offset in the kernel, i.e. a spurious permanent memory

gibbs_ringing_from_the_slow_tail.symptom: a 1.6e-3 plateau at large |t|, on BOTH sides of the origin
gibbs_ringing_from_the_slow_tail.cause: S = T - 1 decays only as -i c/w, so a truncated transform rings
gibbs_ringing_from_the_slow_tail.fix: subtract A(w) = -i c/(w + i a), whose only pole is at w = -ia in the lower half plane so it cannot introduce an acausal piece, and add back its closed-form transform -c e^{-at} theta(t); the remainder decays like 1/w^2
gibbs_ringing_from_the_slow_tail.would_have_been_read_as: a late-time tail -- the very quantity this round would most like to measure, which is exactly why the gate mattered

detail.the_general_point: A quantity that is exactly zero on part of its domain is worth more than an accuracy claim: it calibrates the noise floor for free, on the same run, with no reference value. Both artefacts above sat at the level of the physics being looked for, and neither was visible from the t > 0 side alone.

entries.claim: the retarded outer-to-inner transfer kernel exists as a computable object
entries.evidence: K = delta(t) + K_reg from T(w) on a well-conditioned real-frequency scattering problem

entries.claim: the frequency domain can be used here despite PR #270's and #274's shooting failures
entries.evidence: those failed for Im w < 0, where one solution grows exponentially; for real w nothing dominates, and unitarity holds to ~1e-13 without being imposed
K(t < 0) measured directly; the residual doubles as the noise floor for t > 0

entries.claim: the kernel carries the published ringdown
entries.evidence: fitted against the EXTERNAL continued-fraction value: real part within 0.062%-1.17%, damping 0.11%-3.80% over nine extraction settings; band reported, not best row

entries.claim: an independent method reproduces the kernel
entries.evidence: convolution against PR #274's time-domain characteristic evolution, which shares no code with the transfer matrix
int K_reg dt = -1 exactly (sum rule from T(0) = 0), so the memory cancels the instantaneous part at DC; int |K_reg| dt = 2.02 against the delta's 1

entries.claim: the late-time power-law tail is measured
entries.evidence: the ringdown reaches the ~1e-6 causality noise floor by t ~ 40; a tail would be orders of magnitude below it. No exponent is quoted

entries.claim: PR #274's pulse placement was adequate for this object
entries.verdict: NO -- AND IT WAS FOR ITS OWN
entries.evidence: launching at r* = 6 (V ~ 0.1) gives a 43% mismatch here and was harmless for the quasinormal frequency; a transmission ratio needs an asymptotic launch

detail.the_lesson_this_round_adds: An exactly-zero region is a free error bar. Causality gave this round a stretch of the domain where the answer is known to be zero, on the same run and with no external reference, and two separate artefacts -- a missing DC cell and Gibbs ringing -- were caught there at exactly the amplitude of the physics being sought. PR #274 needed a published spectrum to find its floor; here the structure of the problem supplied one.
detail.the_next_object: The late-time tail, which needs a method with dynamic range where this one has none -- a long time-domain evolution in extended precision rather than a refinement of the frequency-domain route. Separately: whether any BAM exchange kernel is intended to approximate this object, which is a modelling question and not a numerical one.
detail.still_blocked: The nonlinear backreaction oracle, by the C(v) / inner-flux issue, unchanged and unrelated to anything here.
